13thJune2023 KERALAGAZETTE 89 THEHIGHCOURTOFKERALA NOTIFICATION No.DI-1/104010/2019 6thJune2023 InexerciseofthepowersconferredbyArticle225oftheConstitutionofIndia,Section122of theCodeof CivilProcedure,1908(CentralAct5of1908)andofallotherpowershereuntoenabling itin thisbehalf,theHigh CourtofKerala,afterpreviouspublication of the draftRulesin theKerala GazetteVol.Xl,No.34,dated 23rdAugust,2022 as NotificationNo.DI-1/40160/2018,dated 29thJuly2022and inKeralaGazetteVol.XI,No.42,dated 18thOctober,2022asNotification No.D1-1/104010/2019,dated14thSeptember,2022,noobjection or suggestionhavingbeenreceived thereon,andwiththepreviousapprovalof theGovernmentof Keralaconveyedin G.O.(Rt.)No.1269/2023/HOME dated 19-5-2023,hereby makes thefollowingRulesfurther to amend theRules oftheHigh Court ofKerala,1971,namely: RULES 1.ShorttitleandCommencement.—
(1)Theserules shall be called theRules of theHigh Court of Kerala(Second Amendment),2023.
(2)They shall come into force at once. 2.AmendmentoftheRule.— In theRules of theHigh Court ofKerala,1971,—

120292/2026/DISection HCKL/HCKERALA THEHIGHCOURTOFKERALA DI-1/100071/2024 Date:18-09-2026 NOTIFICATION In exercise of the powers conferred by Article 225 of the Constitution of India read with section 122 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (Central Act 5 of 1908), and of all other powers hereunto enabling it in this behalf, the High Court of Kerala after previous publication of the draft Rules in the Kerala Gazette Vol. XV, No. 8, dated, 24 th February, 2026 as Notification No. DI-1/100071/2024 dated 13t hFebruary, 2026, and having considered the suggestions received and with the previous approval of the Government of Kerala conveyed in, G.O.(Ms.)No. 154/2026/HOME dated 03rd September, 2026 hereby makes the following Rules further to amend the Rules of the High Court of Kerala, 1971, namely: RULES
1. Short title and commencement .- (1) These rules may be called the Rules of the High Court of Kerala (Second Amendment),2026.
(2) They shall come into force at once. 2.Amendment of'the Rules .-(1) In rule 5,
(i). after sub-rule (9), the following sub-rule shall be inserted, namely: - "(9A) "Proceedings" include writs, writ appeals, memoranda of appeals, original petitions, revisions, references, applications, arbitration matters, petitions, interlocutory applications, documents or any applications provided under law or any other cases presented or filed under any law in court by any party or such party's/Parties' Advocate or Advocate Commissioner or other officer of the court.".
(ii). after sub-rule(10), the following sub-rules shall be inserted, namely:- "(10A) Registrar (Case and Court Management) shall be a District Judge with at least 2 years of experience as a District Judge.
(10B) "Registrar's Court" means the Court manned by the Registrar (Case and Court Management) and does not include 'Court' as defined in sub-rule (7) of Rule 5 of the Rules."
(ii). The existing sub-rule (10A) to rule 5 shall be renumbered as (10C). File No. HCKL/11526Bbty5RAieeltrags://compose.kerala.gov.in/ Generated from eOffice by Kevin Raj, ASST-D1-1HCKL, ASST-D1-1 HCKL, HIGH COURT OF KERALA on 25/09/2026 03:22 PM

(7) If the party-in-person fails to appoint a counsel of his choice, the Registrar (Case and Court Management) shall submit a report to the Court as to why the applicant is not competent to appear in-person. The Court may, after considering the report and such other material as it deems fit and proper, permit the party-in- person to appear/file/defend and argue the case in person or may decline permission to the party-in- person and may appoint an Advocate as amicus curiae or one from the panel of advocates of High Court Legal Services Committee, for better assistance of the Court and for proper adjudication of the case.
(8) If the Registrar (Case and Court Management) is of the opinion that the party-in-person is competent to assist the Court, he shall guide the party-in-person about the language, demeanor, and decorum to be maintained in the court and shall require the party - in-person to give an undertaking that he/she shall maintain the decorum of the Court and shall not use any objectionable language or behaviour during the course of hearing in the Court or in the Court premises or in the further pleadings."
